questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to review on the touchstone of the basic structure, as held in:

options.A: Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan (1965)
options.B: State of Bihar v. Kameshwar Singh (1952)
options.C: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951)
options.D: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007)

questions.explanation: A nine-judge Bench held that Article 31B immunity does not shield laws that damage the basic structure.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under the doctrine of eclipse, a pre-Constitution law inconsistent with a Fundamental Right is:

options.A: Enforceable only in the State that originally enacted it
options.B: Dormant, not dead, until the inconsistency is removed
options.C: Void from its inception for all purposes and persons
options.D: Permanently repealed with effect from commencement

questions.explanation: In Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of M.P., the law was held to be overshadowed rather than void, and revived once the inconsistency ceased.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The doctrine of 'pith and substance' is applied to decide:

options.A: Whether a statute is retrospective in operation or not
options.B: Whether a law violates the procedure under Article 21
options.C: Which legislature is competent where entries in the Lists overlap
options.D: Whether the President has assented to a Bill

questions.explanation: The Court looks at the true nature and character of the law to determine its legislative competence.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In T.K. Rangarajan v. Government of Tamil Nadu, the Supreme Court held that government employees have:

options.B: A fundamental right to strike subject to public order
options.C: A fundamental right to strike under Article 19(1)(c)
options.D: A fundamental right to strike only in essential services

questions.explanation: The right to form associations does not include a right to strike, which is at best a statutory or moral right.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 22(4), a person cannot be preventively detained beyond three months without the opinion of:
questions.explanation: The Advisory Board consists of persons qualified to be High Court Judges.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Passive euthanasia and 'living wills' were recognised as part of the right to die with dignity under Article 21 in:

options.A: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018)
options.B: Naresh Marotrao Sakhare v. Union of India (1995)
options.C: P. Rathinam v. Union of India (1994)
options.D: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab (1996)

questions.explanation: A Constitution Bench held that the right to life includes the right to die with dignity in cases of terminal illness.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The right of voters to cast a 'None of the Above' (NOTA) vote was recognised in:

options.A: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (2002)
options.B: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India (2013)
options.C: Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006)
options.D: Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013)

questions.explanation: The Court held that negative voting promotes free expression and the secrecy of the ballot.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: A Judge of the Supreme Court can be removed from office only on the ground of:

options.A: Loss of confidence of the Council of Ministers
options.C: A resolution of the Bar Council of India
options.D: Pendency of a criminal case against him

questions.explanation: Article 124(4) requires an address by each House, supported by a special majority, presented to the President.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: A Judge of a High Court holds office until the age of:
questions.explanation: Article 217 sets sixty-two years for High Court Judges, while Supreme Court Judges retire at sixty-five.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Under Article 280, the President constitutes a Finance Commission at the expiration of every:
questions.explanation: The Commission recommends the distribution of tax proceeds between the Union and the States.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In In re: Article 370 of the Constitution (December 2023), the Supreme Court held that the abrogation of Article 370 was:
questions.explanation: A Constitution Bench upheld the Presidential Orders of 2019 and the reorganisation of the State into Union Territories.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The maxim 'what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly' underlies the doctrine of:
questions.explanation: A legislature cannot do indirectly, under the guise of a competent entry, what it is not allowed to do directly.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The 103rd Amendment, providing 10% reservation for economically weaker sections, was upheld in:

options.A: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
options.B: Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008)
options.C: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)
options.D: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)

questions.explanation: A Constitution Bench upheld the amendment by a 3:2 majority.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Hugo Grotius is regarded as the father of:
questions.explanation: His De Jure Belli ac Pacis (1625) laid the foundation of modern international law.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The concept of 'living law' is associated with:
questions.explanation: Ehrlich held that the centre of gravity of legal development lies in society, not in legislation or judicial decisions.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: 'Jus in re aliena' refers to rights:

options.A: Available only to aliens in a State
options.B: Over the property of another person
options.C: Of a person over his own property
options.D: Arising only from a sale contract

questions.explanation: Mortgages, leases and easements are examples of rights in the property of another.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: A 'legal fiction' is:

options.A: An assumption of truth though it may be untrue
options.B: A false statement made in court to deceive the judge
options.C: A rule which bars proof of any fact
options.D: A statute declared void by the court

questions.explanation: Legal fictions, such as adoption creating a parent-child relationship, serve to advance justice.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The Hart–Devlin debate concerned:
questions.explanation: Following the Wolfenden Report, Lord Devlin defended, and Hart opposed, enforcement of morality by criminal law.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Aristotle's classification of justice distinguishes distributive justice from:
questions.explanation: Distributive justice allocates honours and goods; corrective justice rectifies wrongs between persons.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Vicarious liability means the liability:

options.A: Of a person for his own intentional wrong
options.B: Arising only on a criminal conviction
options.C: Of one person for the wrongful act of another
options.D: Without any wrongful act by anyone

questions.explanation: An employer is liable for the torts of an employee committed in the course of employment.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In an auction sale, the bid made by a bidder is regarded in law as:
questions.explanation: The auctioneer invites offers, and the fall of the hammer is acceptance (Section 64, Sale of Goods Act).

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 2(d) of the Indian Contract Act, past consideration is:
questions.explanation: The words 'has done or abstained from doing' include past acts, unlike the English rule.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 5 of the Indian Contract Act, a proposal may be revoked at any time before:

options.A: Consideration is paid by the proposee in full
options.B: The proposee reads and understands the letter
options.C: Its acceptance is complete as against the proposer
options.D: It reaches the person to whom it is addressed and is read

questions.explanation: Once acceptance is complete against the proposer, the proposal can no longer be revoked.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In Derry v. Peek, fraud was defined as a false statement made knowingly, without belief in its truth, or:

options.A: Recklessly, careless whether it be true or false
options.C: Under a bona fide mistake of law

questions.explanation: Derry v. Peek (1889) held that an honest belief, however unreasonable, negates fraud.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: Under Section 12 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, breach of a warranty entitles the buyer only to:

options.B: Rescind the contract and recover the price
options.C: Reject the goods and repudiate the contract
options.D: Refuse payment of the whole price

questions.explanation: Breach of a condition may allow repudiation, but breach of a warranty gives a claim for damages alone.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 25 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, every partner is liable for the acts of the firm:

options.A: Only if he signed the contract
options.B: Only in proportion to his profit share
options.C: Only to the extent of his capital

questions.explanation: A third party may recover the full amount from any partner personally.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Substitution of a new contract for an existing one, with the consent of all parties, is called:
questions.explanation: Section 62 of the Indian Contract Act: the original contract need not then be performed.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Trespass to land is actionable:

options.A: Only on proof of actual loss
options.B: Per se, without proof of damage

questions.explanation: Every unauthorised entry on another's land is actionable even if no harm results.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: A statement made in the course of proceedings in Parliament enjoys:

options.C: Privilege only if made without malice

questions.explanation: Absolute privilege is a complete defence to defamation, irrespective of malice.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The three-stage test for duty of care (foreseeability, proximity and fair, just and reasonable) was laid down in:

options.B: Hedley Byrne & Co. v. Heller & Partners
options.C: Anns v. Merton London Borough Council

questions.explanation: Caparo (1990) replaced the broad two-stage approach of Anns.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: As a general rule, an employer is NOT vicariously liable for the torts of:

options.A: A servant acting in the course of employment
options.C: A partner in the firm's ordinary business
options.D: An agent acting within his authority

questions.explanation: An independent contractor controls how the work is done, though exceptions exist for hazardous work.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Liability for negligent misstatement causing economic loss was established in:

options.A: Hedley Byrne & Co. v. Heller & Partners (1964)
options.D: Overseas Tankship v. Morts Dock Engineering (1961)

questions.explanation: A special relationship and reliance can create a duty to take care in giving advice.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Exemplary damages in tort are intended to:

options.B: Compensate only the actual pecuniary loss

questions.explanation: Rookes v. Barnard limited them to oppressive acts by government servants and conduct calculated to make profit.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Defamation is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 356 corresponds to Section 499 IPC; Section 351 deals with criminal intimidation.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Extortion is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 308 corresponds to Sections 383 and 384 IPC; Section 309 deals with robbery.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: As enacted, Section 106(2) of the BNS punishes a driver who causes death by rash driving and flees without reporting, with imprisonment up to:
questions.explanation: This is a new provision on 'hit and run', whose implementation was kept in abeyance after protests.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: A 'terrorist act' is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 113 brings the offence of terrorism into the ordinary penal code; Section 111 deals with organised crime.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Voluntary intoxication is generally:

options.A: A defence only for offences against property
options.C: A complete defence to every offence
options.D: A defence only for first offenders

questions.explanation: Only involuntary intoxication, which renders the person incapable of knowing the nature of the act, is a defence.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: An assembly of at least how many persons, with a common unlawful object, constitutes an unlawful assembly?
questions.explanation: Section 189 BNS (earlier Section 141 IPC) requires five or more persons.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The offence of bigamy does not apply where the first spouse has been continually absent for:

options.B: Five years and not heard of as alive
options.D: Seven years and not heard of as alive

questions.explanation: The exception requires an absence of seven years during which the spouse has not been heard of, with disclosure to the second spouse.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The maxim 'ignorantia juris non excusat' means that:

options.A: Ignorance of the law is no excuse
options.B: A mistake of fact is always punishable
options.C: Ignorance of fact is no excuse

questions.explanation: Every person is presumed to know the law of the land.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 20 of the CPC, a suit may be instituted where the defendant resides or where:

options.A: The cause of action arises wholly or in part
options.B: The plaintiff's advocate ordinarily practises in court
options.D: The High Court chooses to sit

questions.explanation: Section 20 is the residuary provision on territorial jurisdiction for suits not covered by Sections 15 to 19.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A pleading in a civil suit must contain:

options.C: Material facts, but not the evidence
options.D: Evidence, but not the material facts

questions.explanation: Order VI Rule 2 requires a concise statement of the material facts on which the party relies.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: In a summary suit under Order XXXVII of the CPC, the defendant can defend the suit only:

options.B: With the leave of the court
options.C: After depositing the whole decretal amount

questions.explanation: If leave is refused or the defendant fails to apply, the plaintiff is entitled to a decree.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A first appeal from an original decree lies under:
questions.explanation: Section 100 provides for second appeals, Section 104 for appeals from orders and Section 115 for revision.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure deals with:
questions.explanation: Restitution puts the parties back where they were once a decree is varied or reversed.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: In Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar, the Supreme Court directed police not to arrest automatically in offences punishable with imprisonment up to:
questions.explanation: The Court required a notice of appearance and recorded reasons for arrest, now reflected in the BNSS.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Plea bargaining is NOT available for an offence punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment extending up to seven years
options.B: Imprisonment extending up to three years
options.C: Death, life, or over seven years' term
options.D: Imprisonment up to one year or fine only

questions.explanation: It is also barred for offences affecting the socio-economic condition of the country and offences against women or children below fourteen.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 17 of the Limitation Act, 1963, where a suit is based on fraud, limitation starts from the date of:
questions.explanation: Section 17 postpones the start of limitation until the fraud or mistake is discovered.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: An admission under the law of evidence is:

options.A: Always conclusive proof of the whole fact admitted by him
options.D: Not conclusive proof, but may operate as estoppel

questions.explanation: An admission can be explained or rebutted unless it creates an estoppel.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: The opinion of a handwriting expert is, as a rule of prudence:

options.A: Conclusive and binding on the court
options.B: Inadmissible in all cases of disputed writing

questions.explanation: Expert opinion is relevant under Section 45 (Section 39 BSA) but the court is not bound by it.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 112 of the Evidence Act, birth during a valid marriage is conclusive proof of legitimacy unless:

options.D: Non-access between the spouses is proved

questions.explanation: Nandlal Wasudeo Badwaik v. Lata Nandlal held that DNA evidence cannot override the conclusive presumption where access exists.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Under Section 27 of the Evidence Act, information received from an accused in police custody is admissible only to the extent that it:

options.C: Leads to the discovery of a fact

questions.explanation: Pulukuri Kottaya v. Emperor clarified that only the part distinctly relating to the discovery is provable.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Under Article 27 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, a State may not invoke its internal law as:

options.B: A ground for lawfully entering into a treaty
options.C: Evidence of a rule of customary international law
options.D: A justification for failing to perform a treaty

questions.explanation: The rule reinforces pacta sunt servanda.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The right of innocent passage through the territorial sea is available to:

options.A: Only ships of the coastal State
options.B: Only merchant ships of allied States

questions.explanation: UNCLOS Articles 17–19 give ships of all States this right, so long as passage is not prejudicial to the coastal State.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Article 51 of the UN Charter recognises the inherent right of States to:

options.D: Seize foreign vessels on the high seas

questions.explanation: The right lasts until the Security Council takes measures to maintain peace.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The 'Responsibility to Protect' (R2P) doctrine was endorsed by UN member States at the:
questions.explanation: R2P concerns genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Under the doctrine of restrictive immunity, a State is NOT immune for acts:

options.D: Done by its head of State in office

questions.explanation: Immunity is confined to sovereign acts (jure imperii).

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The World Trade Organization came into existence on:
questions.explanation: The WTO replaced the GATT framework following the Uruguay Round.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, desertion is a ground of divorce if continuous for at least:
questions.explanation: Section 13(1)(ib) requires desertion without reasonable cause for a continuous period of not less than two years immediately preceding the petition.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: A valid adoption under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 requires:

options.B: Prior permission of the High Court
options.C: Actual giving and taking of the child
options.D: Registration of the deed before a magistrate

questions.explanation: Section 11(vi): the child must be actually given and taken with intent to transfer the child from the family of its birth.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Talaq-e-ahsan consists of:

options.A: A decree of the court on petition
options.B: A written deed attested by a magistrate
options.C: Three pronouncements made in a single sitting at once
options.D: A single pronouncement in a tuhr followed by iddat

questions.explanation: It is the most approved form of talaq, and the husband can revoke it during iddat.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: A Muslim can bequeath by will, without the consent of the heirs, not more than:
questions.explanation: A bequest above one-third requires the consent of the heirs after the testator's death.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under Section 107 of the TPA, a lease of immovable property from year to year, or for a term exceeding one year, can be made only by:
questions.explanation: Other leases may be made by oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession.

questions.subject: Succession Law
questions.question: In V. Tulasamma v. Sesha Reddy, the Supreme Court held that under Section 14(1) of the HSA, a Hindu woman's limited estate in property given for maintenance becomes:

options.C: An estate for her minor child

questions.explanation: Section 14(1) was held to convert limited estates held in lieu of maintenance into full ownership.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: Under the Designs Act, 2000, registration of a design is initially valid for ten years and extendable by:
questions.explanation: The total period of protection can therefore be fifteen years.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: Under the Copyright Act, 1957, fair dealing with a literary work for private study or research is:

options.A: An infringement if the copy is made for profit
options.B: Permitted only on payment of a licence fee
options.C: An infringement unless the author consents

questions.explanation: Section 52 lists acts which do not constitute infringement.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: The classic definition of 'sustainable development' comes from the 1987 report of the:
questions.explanation: Our Common Future defined it as development that meets present needs without compromising future generations.

questions.subject: Company Law
questions.question: The maximum number of members in a private company under the Companies Act, 2013 is:
questions.explanation: Section 2(68) restricts a private company to 200 members, excluding employee-members and ex-employees.

questions.subject: Administrative Law
questions.question: The doctrine of promissory estoppel was applied against the Government in:

options.B: A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India (1969)
options.C: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)

questions.explanation: The Supreme Court held that the doctrine applies against the Government, and no detriment need be proved.

questions.subject: Insolvency Law
questions.question: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the corporate insolvency resolution process must ordinarily be completed within:
questions.explanation: The overall limit including litigation is 330 days.

questions.subject: Juvenile Justice
questions.question: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a preliminary assessment for being tried as an adult in heinous offences applies to a child aged:
questions.explanation: The Juvenile Justice Board assesses mental and physical capacity and ability to understand consequences.

questions.subject: Arbitration Law
questions.question: An application to set aside an arbitral award under Section 34 must be made within three months, extendable by a further:
questions.explanation: The proviso allows the court to condone delay for up to thirty days on sufficient cause.

questions.subject: Contempt of Courts
questions.question: Under Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, simple imprisonment for contempt may extend to:
questions.explanation: The maximum fine is two thousand rupees; an apology may lead to remission.

questions.subject: Disability Law
questions.question: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, a 'person with benchmark disability' has not less than:

options.A: Twenty per cent of a specified disability
options.B: Sixty per cent of a specified disability
options.C: Eighty per cent of a specified disability
options.D: Forty per cent of a specified disability

questions.explanation: Persons with benchmark disabilities are entitled to reservation in jobs and education.
